review_type: Shared firmware-data lifetime and proc read/write concurrency review

branch_context.scope_note: This review records a residual race on the hardening branch. It does not modify the stock-exact reconstruction or claim that the retry hardening fixes concurrent lifetime access.

entrypoints: sysfs binary attribute fwimage read and write
scope.analysis_basis: Reconstructed C and AArch64 inline assembly, Ghidra stock decompilation/call references, source registration, and the target kernel source in the canonical Docker volume

target_kernel.proc_dispatch_observation: proc_reg_read/proc_reg_write enter pde_read/pde_write, which directly invokes proc_ops callbacks. The shown dispatch path has no per-entry callback serialization; vfs_write directly invokes file->f_op->write.

findings.details: tp_self_test_write allocates the shared descriptor, invokes the test callback at cdev+0xfa0, and the three testing routines later call tpd_copy_to_tp_firmware_data. Concurrently, tp_self_test_read invokes the separate show callback at cdev+0xf98 and then frees cdev+0xc58 unconditionally. The read handler does not take the existing mutex. The writer's copy helper reloads the global pointer with READ_ONCE but has no lifetime reference or lock before dereferencing data and calling memcpy; the write handler also dereferences the slot at its epilogue without a null check. A read can therefore free the descriptor or data during a writer operation. This is a reachable race window, not a claim that every overlap crashes.
evidence: zte_touch_probe.c:323 registers tp_self_test with mode 0664; globals.c:2073 binds proc_read and proc_write to tp_self_test_read and tp_self_test_write.
syna_tpd_register_fw_class.c:121-122 installs tpd_test_cmd_store and tpd_test_cmd_show at cdev offsets 0xfa0 and 0xf98.
tp_self_test_read.c frees the object at cdev+0xc58 after tpd_test_cmd_show; it does not acquire cdev+0xc60.
tp_self_test_write.c allocates, invokes the store callback, then dereferences cdev+0xc58 at the handler epilogue.
Ghidra calls.jsonl records tpd_copy_to_tp_firmware_data callers syna_testing_pt01_zte, syna_testing_pt05_zte, and syna_testing_pt0a_zte.
Target kernel commit 3356b353 proc_reg_read/proc_reg_write directly dispatches proc_ops callbacks without a driver-state lock.

findings.details: Several firmware and noise handlers use cdev+0xc60, but probe initializes that offset as ztp_dev->cmd_mutex. tp_alloc_tp_firmware_data, tpd_copy_to_tp_firmware_data, tp_self_test_read and tp_self_test_write do not use it. The fwimage sysfs handlers perform initial descriptor/data/size checks before taking cmd_mutex, then reload and dereference the slot after locking without revalidating null. Thus existing locking does not establish a lifetime contract for the shared pointer.
evidence: zte_touch_probe.c:270 initializes offset 3168 (0xc60) with label ztp_dev->cmd_mutex.
get_tp_noise_show.c, get_tp_noise_store.c, tpfwupgrade_store.c and parts of tpd_sysfs_fwimage_show/store use cdev+0xc60.
tp_alloc_tp_firmware_data.c, tpd_copy_to_tp_firmware_data.c and tp_self_test_read.c access or free cdev+0xc58 without that mutex.
tpd_sysfs_fwimage_show.c and tpd_sysfs_fwimage_store.c dereference the slot before acquiring cdev+0xc60.

recommendation: Keep the vmalloc-failure retry fix as a separate hardening deviation. For the concurrency issue, first audit every cdev+0xc58/cdev+0x448 access and establish one dedicated firmware-buffer lifetime lock/reference contract across allocation, copy, read cleanup, sysfs binary I/O, noise handlers, firmware upgrade, reset/free helpers, and the writer epilogue. Do not hold cmd_mutex across the full test callback: its declared role is command serialization and nested test-command locking must be checked to avoid deadlock. Implement this as a new hardening batch, validate it in the canonical Docker workspace, and keep the stock-exact branch unchanged.
